mainTopic: Sources for disqualifying a מחוסר כיפורים and an unwashed כהן, and the laws of washing hands and feet: when it is essential, how it is done, and how long it lasts.
overview: The amud opens with the last words of an earlier answer: the כהן גדול's תפילין sat in a gap on his head, so they did not block his garment. The גמרא then gives sources for two invalid cases from the משנה. A מחוסר כיפורים is still partly טמא, learned from "וטהרה". A כהן who did not wash is learned from חוקה–חוקה with מחוסר בגדים. A ברייתא teaches that skipping the extra יום כיפור immersions and washings does not ruin the service, but skipping the morning washing does. רב אסי asks why, and after רבי יוחנן's answer falls, חזקיה and רבי יונתן each bring a פסוק showing that the כהן גדול follows the rules of regular כהנים. Next comes how the washing is done: standing, with hands on feet, and the חכמים and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה argue over a stacked position held up with help. Finally, רבי and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון argue whether the passing of night ends a washing, using the words בגשתם and בבואם. The amud ends by asking what the words להקטיר אשה add, and the answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: The תפילין were worn in the gap
steps.stepSummary: These are the closing words of the previous answer: the כהן גדול put his תפילין in the space on his head that was left open.
steps.simpleTranslation: For that is where they put on תפילין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an answer it began before this section. It explains that the תפילין sat in an open spot on the head, so they did not come between the כהן's head and his priestly head covering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry was that the תפילין של ראש might block the priestly garment from touching the head. This line removes that worry: the תפילין went in a gap that the garment did not cover. So there is no blocking, and the service stays valid.

keyTerms.meaning: Leather boxes holding פסוקים, worn on the head and arm

phrases.english: For it is there that they put on tefillin.
phrases.notes: "There" means the open space on the head discussed just before, between the ציץ and the מצנפת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes an answer that started earlier on the daf.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual clarification of where the item was placed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think the תפילין come between the garment and the head and make the service invalid.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תפילין sat in a gap the garment did not cover, so nothing comes between them.

steps.title: Source for the one who has not brought his atonement offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn that a מחוסר כיפורים may not do the service.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person still missing his atonement offering: from where do we know his service is invalid?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the list of invalid people in the משנה and asks for the source for one of them. This sets up רב הונא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מחוסר כיפורים has already immersed and waited until nightfall, but he has not yet brought his offering. The question is why such a person should count as unfit to serve, so the גמרא wants a פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who still needs to bring his atonement offering to finish becoming pure
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: One lacking atonement, from where do we derive this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: sources for the משנה's invalid categories.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that makes a מחוסר כיפורים unfit to do the service.

steps.title: רב הונא: "she shall be pure" shows she was still impure
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא learns from the פסוק about a יולדת's offering. Since the פסוק says she becomes pure only after the offering, she must still be partly טמא until then.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: the פסוק says, "And the כהן shall make atonement for her, and she shall be pure." If she becomes pure only now, she must have been impure until now.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers the question with a פסוק about a woman after childbirth. The words "she shall be pure" show she was not fully pure before her offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word טהרה, "she shall be pure", comes after the offering. That teaches that before the offering she still had some טומאה, even though she had already immersed. We already know that someone who is טמא may not do the service, so a מחוסר כיפורים is also unfit.

keyTerms.meaning: By inference, from what it implies

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean the person is fully טמא like before immersion. He is only partly impure until he brings the offering, and that is enough to make him unfit to serve.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said: The verse states:
"And the priest shall make atonement for her, and she shall be pure"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 12:8

phrases.english: "She shall be pure": by inference, she is now impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק "וכפר עליה הכהן וטהרה" shows she is still partly טמא until her offering. So a מחוסר כיפורים counts as טמא and his service is invalid.

steps.title: Unwashed hands and feet: learned from "חוקה"
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next case in the משנה, a כהן who did not wash his hands and feet. It learns this from a גזירה שווה on the word חוקה, which also appears with מחוסר בגדים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one whose hands and feet are not washed: this is learned from the word "חוקה" here and the word "חוקה" used for a כהן missing his garments.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the next invalid person from the משנה and gives the source right away. It links the two cases through a shared word, חוקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know that a כהן missing his priestly garments may not serve. Both topics use the word חוקה, so the rule carries over through a גזירה שווה. A כהן who did not wash is therefore also unfit, just like one missing his garments.

keyTerms.meaning: Washed hands and feet, done from the כיור before the service
It is learned from, comes from
A כהן missing his priestly garments

steps.whatToRemember: Each invalid case has its own source. מחוסר כיפורים is learned from "וטהרה" (he is still partly טמא). Not washing is learned from חוקה–חוקה with מחוסר בגדים.

phrases.english: And one whose hands and feet are not washed.
phrases.notes: This is the משנה's next case. The question "where do we learn it from?" is left unsaid, but we're meant to hear it.

phrases.english: It is derived from "statute"–"statute" from one lacking garments.
phrases.notes: The word חוקה appears both with washing and with the priestly garments, so the rule moves from one to the other.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same pattern as steps 2–3, now for the next case in the משנה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שווה of חוקה–חוקה from מחוסר בגדים.

steps.title: Skipping the extra washings on יום כיפור: service still valid
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that if the כהן גדול did not immerse or wash between garment changes or between services, his service is still valid after the fact.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: a כהן גדול who did not immerse and did not wash, between one set of garments and the next or between one service and the next, and then served: his service is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that limits the washing rule. Missing the extra immersions and washings of the יום כיפור service does not make the service invalid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום כיפור the כהן גדול immerses and washes each time he switches between gold and white garments. These are required, but skipping them does not invalidate the service after the fact. So not every missed washing makes the service invalid.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל שֶׁלֹּא טָבַל וְשֶׁלֹּא קִידֵּשׁ
phrases.english: A High Priest who did not immerse and did not sanctify

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין בֶּגֶד לְבֶגֶד וּבֵין עֲבוֹדָה לַעֲבוֹדָה,
phrases.english: between garment and garment, and between rite and rite,
phrases.notes: This is the יום כיפור service, when he switches between the gold garments and the white linen ones.

phrases.english: and he performed the service: his service is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the washing rule from step 4: skipping the in-between washings does not invalidate the service.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the כהן גדול skips the immersions and washings between garments or between services on יום כיפור, his service is still valid after the fact.

steps.title: No morning washing at all: service invalid
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. Any כהן, גדול or regular, who did not wash his hands and feet in the morning at all, and served, has invalid service.
steps.simpleTranslation: But whether a כהן גדול or a regular כהן: if he did not wash his hands and feet in the morning and then served, his service is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The same ברייתא now gives the other side. The first washing of the day is essential, and without it the service is invalid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This step shows where the rule from step 4 really applies. The basic morning washing makes the service invalid if it is missing, for every כהן. Only the extra washings of יום כיפור are not essential after the fact.

keyTerms.meaning: An ordinary כהן, not the כהן גדול

steps.whatToRemember: The morning washing is essential for every כהן, so without it the service is invalid. The extra washings between garments or services on יום כיפור are required, but skipping them does not invalidate the service after the fact.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶחָד כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל וְאֶחָד כֹּהֵן הֶדְיוֹט
phrases.english: But both a High Priest and an ordinary priest
who did not sanctify his hands and feet in the morning,
and he performed the service: his service is disqualified.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶחָד כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל וְאֶחָד כֹּהֵן הֶדְיוֹט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second half of the same ברייתא, contrasting with step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any כהן who did not wash his hands and feet in the morning and then served has invalid service.

steps.title: רב אסי challenges: the immersions and washings should be required
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי asks רבי יוחנן why the five טבילות and ten קידושין of יום כיפור do not hold back the service. They are from the Torah, and the Torah calls them a חוקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי said to רבי יוחנן: The five immersions and ten washings are from the תורה, and the word 'statute' is written about them. So they should be required, and skipping them should ruin the service!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אסי challenges the ברייתא from Step 5, which said that skipping the immersions and washings does not ruin the service.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Back in Step 4, the word חוקה taught that something is required, meaning that without it the service does not count. The word חוקה also appears in the יום כיפור section. So by the same logic, every immersion and washing should be required.

keyTerms.meaning: Here: washing the hands and feet from the כיור
They should hold back the service, meaning without them it does not count
Now, since (opens an argument based on known facts)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַסִּי לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rav Asi said to Rabbi Yochanan:
Now, the five immersions
phrases.notes: On יום כיפור the כהן גדול immerses each time he changes his clothes, and washes his hands and feet twice for each change.

phrases.english: and ten washings are from the Torah,
and 'statute' is written about them,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 16:34

phrases.english: so they should be required!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּדִי חָמֵשׁ טְבִילוֹת וַעֲשָׂרָה קִדּוּשִׁין דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of the ברייתא in Step 5
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that missed immersions and washings do not ruin the יום כיפור service
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word חוקה signals that something is required (Step 4), and חוקה is written about the יום כיפור service, so these acts should be required too.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: only wearing the garments is required
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers from the word ולבשם that only wearing the garments holds back the service. Nothing else does.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The verse says 'and put them on.' Wearing the garments is required, but nothing else is required.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers רב אסי with a פסוק that limits what is required.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra word ולבשם is read as narrowing the rule: on יום כיפור only the garments are required. That would explain why skipping the immersions and washings does not ruin the service, even though חוקה is written.

keyTerms.meaning: And he shall put them on
Holds back the service, meaning it is required

phrases.english: He said to him: The verse says:
'and put them on,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 16:4

phrases.english: wearing is required,
and nothing else is required.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אסי's challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting derivation from an extra word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: חוקה makes every immersion and washing required
steps.terutzMaskana: ולבשם limits the requirement to wearing the garments alone

steps.title: רבי יוחנן admits his answer does not work
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי is happy with the answer, but רבי יוחנן tells him it is weak. If only the garments were required, the morning washing would also not be required, yet Step 6 says it is.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי's face lit up. רבי יוחנן said to him: I have only written a vav on a beam for you. If so, the morning washing would also not be required!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן knocks down his own answer from Step 8.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ולבשם answer proves too much. It would mean no washing is ever required on יום כיפור, but the ברייתא in Step 6 says that skipping the morning washing does ruin the service. So the answer cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: His face lit up with joy
On a beam or piece of wood

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up who is speaking. רב אסי is the one smiling, and רבי יוחנן is the one who rejects his own answer.

phrases.english: His face lit up.
phrases.notes: This is רב אסי.

phrases.english: He said to him:
I have written a vav on a beam for you,
phrases.notes: He means: this answer is flimsy and won't hold up.

phrases.english: If so, the morning one too.
phrases.notes: The morning washing wouldn't be required either, which goes against Step 6.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 8
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It would also excuse the morning washing, which Step 6 says is required

steps.title: חזקיה: the כהן גדול follows the rules of regular כהנים
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה learns from לו ולזרעו that whatever is required for regular כהנים is required for the כהן גדול, and whatever is not required for them is not required for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: חזקיה said: The פסוק says, 'And it shall be a statute forever to them, to him and to his seed throughout their generations.' Something required for his descendants is required for him. Something not required for his descendants is not required for him.
steps.whatsHappening: חזקיה gives a new answer that explains both rulings of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק compares אהרן to his descendants. Regular כהנים must wash in the morning, so the morning washing is required for the כהן גדול too (Step 6). Regular כהנים never wash between each service, so on יום כיפור those extra washings are not required (Step 5).

keyTerms.meaning: To him (אהרן) and to his descendants
That holds back the service, meaning it is required

steps.whatToRemember: The כהן גדול's required acts match those of regular כהנים. The morning washing is required. The extra immersions and washings of יום כיפור are not required, because regular כהנים never do them.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer fits both rulings of the ברייתא, which רבי יוחנן's answer could not do.

phrases.english: Chizkiya said: The verse says:
'And it shall be a statute forever to them,'
'to him and to his seed throughout their generations,'
phrases.notes: שמות 30:21, a פסוק about washing hands and feet.

phrases.english: something that is required for his seed
phrases.notes: 'His seed' means the regular כהנים, and 'him' means the כהן גדול.

phrases.english: is required for him;
something that is not required for his seed
is not required for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר חִזְקִיָּה, אָמַר קְרָא: וְהָיְתָה לָהֶם חׇק עוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new answer after the answer of Step 8 was rejected
steps.terutzResolutionType: Comparison between the כהן גדול and regular כהנים based on the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: חוקה makes every יום כיפור washing required
steps.terutzMaskana: Only what is required for regular כהנים, like the morning washing, is required for the כהן גדול

steps.title: רבי יונתן's different source for the same rule
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן learns from the פסוק "ורחצו ממנו משה ואהרן ובניו" that whatever holds back the service of the sons also holds back the service of אהרן, and whatever does not hold back theirs does not hold back his.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יונתן says we learn it from here: "משה and אהרן and his sons washed from it." Something that holds back the service of his sons holds back his service. Something that does not hold back his sons' service does not hold back his.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives his own answer to רב אסי's question. He teaches the same rule as חזקיה but from a different פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק puts אהרן (the כהן גדול) and his sons (regular כהנים) together in one washing. So they share the same rules. The morning washing holds back regular כהנים, so it holds back the כהן גדול too. The extra יום כיפור washings do not apply to regular כהנים, so they do not hold back the כהן גדול either.

keyTerms.meaning: and they washed from it (from the כיור)
holds back; without it the service is invalid
his sons, meaning the regular כהנים

phrases.english: Rabbi Yonatan said: from here.
"And Moshe and Aharon and his sons washed from it"
phrases.notes: שמות 40:31. "It" is the כיור, the washing basin in the מקדש.

phrases.english: something that holds back the service of his sons holds back his service,

phrases.aramaic: דָּבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְעַכֵּב בְּבָנָיו אֵין מְעַכֵּב בּוֹ.
phrases.english: something that does not hold back his sons' service does not hold back his.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second source for the rule חזקיה taught in Step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative פסוק for the same principle
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think every יום כיפור washing holds back the כהן גדול, since the Torah calls it a חוקה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only what holds back regular כהנים holds back the כהן גדול. That includes the morning washing but not the extra יום כיפור washings.

steps.title: Why doesn't רבי יונתן use חזקיה's פסוק?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יונתן did not learn the rule from חזקיה's source, לו ולזרעו.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason רבי יונתן did not say it from חזקיה's source?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a comparison between the two sources. It first asks why רבי יונתן did not use חזקיה's words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If לו ולזרעו already teaches the rule, רבי יונתן should not need a new פסוק. The question assumes he must have a reason to reject that source.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yonatan, what is the reason
he did not say it from Chizkiya's source?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר מִדְּחִזְקִיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares רבי יונתן's source with חזקיה's source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי יונתן does not accept לו ולזרעו as the source.

steps.title: חזקיה's פסוק teaches that the law lasts for all generations
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן would say that the words לו ולזרעו come to teach that the law lasts for all future generations. They do not compare the כהן גדול to regular כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would tell you: that phrase is written to teach that the law applies for all generations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי יונתן. He uses חזקיה's words for a different lesson.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יונתן, "him and his descendants" means the washing law is not only for אהרן's lifetime but forever. Those words are already used up, so he needs a different פסוק for the comparison.

keyTerms.meaning: for all generations; for the future

phrases.english: He would tell you:
that one is written to teach about all generations.
phrases.notes: "That one" means לו ולזרעו, the words חזקיה used in Step 10.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ הָהוּא לְדוֹרוֹת הוּא דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: חזקיה's words are needed to teach that the law applies in every generation.

steps.title: Why doesn't חזקיה use רבי יונתן's פסוק?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now asks the opposite question: why didn't חזקיה learn the rule from רבי יונתן's פסוק?
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one, what is the reason he did not say it from this פסוק?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the question around. Now it asks about חזקיה's side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יונתן's פסוק clearly puts אהרן and his sons together. So the גמרא asks why חזקיה did not simply use it.

phrases.english: And the other one,
phrases.notes: This means חזקיה.

phrases.english: what is the reason he did not say it from this one?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר מֵהַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The opposite of Step 12's question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why חזקיה does not use "ורחצו ממנו משה ואהרן ובניו".

steps.title: The פסוק is needed for the rule of four כהנים
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה needs the פסוק for רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's rule: a כיור without enough water for four כהנים to wash may not be used.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs it for the teaching of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא. רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: any כיור that does not hold enough water for four כהנים to wash from it may not be used, as it says "משה and אהרן and his sons washed from it."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for חזקיה. He uses the פסוק for a different law about the כיור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק names four people washing from the כיור: משה, אהרן, and אהרן's two sons. From this רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא learns the smallest amount of water a כיור must hold. Since the פסוק is used for that law, חזקיה does not take the כהן גדול comparison from it.

keyTerms.meaning: the washing basin in the מקדש
to wash the hands and feet before service

steps.whatToRemember: Each אמורא uses one source for the כהן גדול rule and the other source for a different law. רבי יונתן uses לו ולזרעו for "all generations." חזקיה uses ורחצו ממנו for the four-כהנים amount in the כיור.

phrases.aramaic: מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְכִדְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא –
phrases.english: He needs it for the teaching of Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina,
as Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina said:
any basin that does not have in it
enough for four kohanim to wash from it,
one may not wash with it,
as it says: "And Moshe and Aharon and his sons washed from it."
phrases.notes: Count them: משה, אהרן, and his two sons. That makes four.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְכִדְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק is used for the rule that the כיור must hold enough water for four כהנים.

steps.title: How the washing is done: right hand on right foot
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches the method of washing: the כהן places his right hand on his right foot and his left hand on his left foot, and then washes.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: How is the מצוה of washing done? He places his right hand on top of his right foot and his left hand on top of his left foot, and washes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It brings a ברייתא that describes how a כהן washes his hands and feet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hands and feet are washed together. Each hand rests on the foot on the same side, and the water from the כיור runs over both at once.

keyTerms.meaning: the מצוה of washing hands and feet

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
How is the מצוה of washing done?

phrases.aramaic: מַנִּיחַ יָדוֹ הַיְמָנִית עַל גַּבֵּי רַגְלוֹ הַיְמָנִית,
phrases.english: He places his right hand on top of his right foot,

phrases.aramaic: וְיָדוֹ הַשְּׂמָאלִית עַל גַּבֵּי רַגְלוֹ הַשְּׂמָאלִית,
phrases.english: and his left hand on top of his left foot,
and washes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic: the practical method of the washing discussed earlier.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each hand is placed on the foot on its own side, and they are washed together.

steps.title: רבי יוסי son of רבי יהודה: all hands and feet stacked together
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says the כהן stacks both hands one on the other, places them on both feet stacked one on the other, and washes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says: he places his two hands one on top of the other, on top of his two feet one on top of the other, and washes.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion in the ברייתא gives a different way to wash.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this method, all four limbs are washed in one stack: one foot on the other foot, and both hands on top. This disagrees with the first opinion, where each side is washed separately.

keyTerms.meaning: one on top of the other

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: מַנִּיחַ שְׁתֵּי יָדָיו זוֹ עַל גַּב זוֹ,
phrases.english: He places his two hands one on top of the other,

phrases.aramaic: וְעַל גַּבֵּי שְׁתֵּי רַגְלָיו זוֹ עַל גַּבֵּי זוֹ,
phrases.english: on top of his two feet, one on top of the other,
and washes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the method given in Step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both hands and both feet are stacked together and washed at once.

steps.title: The Sages reject this method as impossible
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים tell רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה that he has gone too far, because no one can actually wash that way.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: You have gone too far; it is impossible to do that.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים push back against רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's method.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their objection is practical. A person cannot stand with one foot on top of the other, bend down, and stack both hands on them, so the method cannot be carried out.

keyTerms.meaning: you have gone too far; you exaggerated

phrases.english: They said to him: You have gone too far,
it is impossible to do so.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the method of Step 17.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's method of stacking all four limbs.

steps.title: The גמרא agrees the Sages' objection is strong
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the חכמים spoke well: the stacked-hands position really does seem impossible.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are speaking well to him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sides with the חכמים' complaint against רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. This sets up the next move, where someone has to defend his opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 18 the חכמים said nobody can wash with hands and feet stacked. Now the גמרא itself agrees that this is a real problem. So the method of רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה needs an explanation.

phrases.english: They are speaking well to him!
phrases.notes: "They" are the חכמים, and "him" is רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה from the step before.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Endorses the חכמים' rejection in Step 18 and sharpens it into a real difficulty.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's stacked-hands-and-feet method of washing
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Standing with both feet stacked and both hands stacked on top seems physically impossible, so how could this be the required method?

steps.title: Another כהן helps him keep his balance
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains that a second כהן holds up the washing כהן so the stacked position is possible.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: And his fellow כהן helps him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף defends רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. The washing is possible because a friend supports the כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was balance, not the method itself. With another כהן steadying him, the כהן can stack his feet and hands and wash. So the method is no longer impossible.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: And his fellow helps him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty of Step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifying the case: the position is held with outside help
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The stacked position is impossible, so רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's view cannot work.
steps.terutzMaskana: It works because another כהן holds him steady while he washes.

steps.title: What is the practical difference between the two views?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what actually separates the חכמים from רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where the two opinions lead to a different result. This sets up אביי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree the כהן washes hands and feet. Since רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's method can now work with help, the גמרא wants to know what real case they argue about.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the defense in Step 20, the גמרא asks for the practical outcome of the dispute.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical case in which the חכמים and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה would rule differently.

steps.title: They argue about standing with support from the side
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the difference is whether standing while being held up from the side counts as standing.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Standing from the side is the difference between them.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question. The two views argue about a כהן who stands only because someone supports him from the side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's method needs a helper, so he holds that supported standing still counts as standing. The חכמים do not count it as real standing, so the כהן may not wash that way.

keyTerms.meaning: From the side (held up by support)

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Standing from the side is between them.
phrases.notes: He means standing while someone else props you up from the side.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: עֲמִידָה מִן הַצַּד אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The views differ on whether standing with support from the side counts as standing for washing.
steps.whatToRemember: Washing at the כיור must be done standing. The חכמים and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה argue whether standing while being held up counts.

steps.title: Why not let him sit and wash?
steps.stepSummary: רב סמא בריה דרב אשי asks רבינא why the כהן doesn't simply sit down and wash all at once.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב סמא בריה דרב אשי said to רבינא: Let him sit down and wash!
steps.whatsHappening: A new challenge: if balance is the problem, why not wash while sitting? This sets up רבינא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sitting would solve the balance problem, and the כהן could reach his hands and feet together easily. The question assumes nothing requires standing for washing.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב סַמָּא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אָשֵׁי לְרָבִינָא:
phrases.english: Rav Samma, son of Rav Ashi, said to Ravina:
And let him sit and sanctify!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב סַמָּא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אָשֵׁי לְרָבִינָא: וְלִיתֵּיב מִיתָּב וּלְקַדֵּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the whole need for standing, which Steps 20 to 22 assumed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that washing must be done standing
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If sitting were allowed, there would be no balance problem and no need for a helper.

steps.title: Washing is for service, and service is done standing
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק links washing to serving, and serving in the מקדש is done standing, so washing must be done standing too.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says "to serve," and service is done standing.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers from a פסוק: washing is connected to service, so it follows the rules of service.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about the כיור speaks of coming near the מזבח "לשרת", to serve. Service in the מקדש is done standing. So washing, which prepares for service, also has to be done standing, and sitting is not allowed.

phrases.english: The verse states: "To minister"
phrases.notes: שמות 30:20

phrases.english: And ministering is done standing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 23.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A כהן could sit while washing to avoid losing his balance.
steps.terutzMaskana: Washing is tied to service, and service is done standing, so washing must be done standing.
steps.whatToRemember: A כהן may not wash his hands and feet sitting down, because washing is part of service, and service is done standing.

steps.title: רבי: night passing ends the washing
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says washing by day covers the following night, but washing at night does not cover the next day, because for רבי the passing of night ends the washing.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא: If a כהן washed his hands and feet by day, he does not need to wash again at night. If he washed at night, he must wash again by day. This is רבי's view, because רבי held that staying overnight ends the washing of hands and feet.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with a ברייתא about how long one washing lasts. This is רבי's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The night goes with the day before it, so washing in the day still counts that night. But once the night passes into a new day, the washing is finished, just like holy items become unfit when left overnight. So a כהן who washed at night must wash again in the morning.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two halves: washing by day DOES cover that night, but washing at night does NOT cover the next day.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: קִידֵּשׁ יָדָיו וְרַגְלָיו בַּיּוֹם –
phrases.english: The Sages taught: If he sanctified his hands and feet in the day,
he does not need to sanctify at night;
if at night, he needs to sanctify in the day.
These are the words of Rebbi, for Rebbi used to say:
Staying overnight takes effect on the sanctification of hands and feet.
phrases.notes: He means the night passing cancels the washing, the way holy things become unfit when left overnight.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: קִידֵּשׁ יָדָיו וְרַגְלָיו בַּיּוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about how long washing at the כיור stays valid.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי, the passing of night ends a כהן's washing, so washing by night must be repeated by day.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר son of רבי שמעון: night does not end the washing
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון disagrees and holds that the passing of night does not cancel the washing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says: Staying overnight does not end the washing of hands and feet.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings the opposing view to רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, the night passing has no effect on the washing. So a כהן who washed at night does not need to wash again the next morning just because a new day started.

keyTerms.meaning: Staying overnight does not take effect (does not cancel)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי: the passing of night ends the washing. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון: it does not.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon, says:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לִינָה מוֹעֶלֶת בְּקִידּוּשׁ יָדַיִם וְרַגְלַיִם.
phrases.english: Staying overnight does not take effect on the sanctification of hands and feet.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: אֵין לִינָה מוֹעֶלֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing opinion to רבי's view in Step 25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The passing of night does not end a כהן's washing of hands and feet.

steps.title: A second ברייתא: serving on the מזבח all night
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that a כהן who served all night must wash again in the morning, according to רבי. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says one washing at the start covers him, even for ten days.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches: if a כהן stood and offered on the מזבח all night, then in the morning he must wash his hands and feet again. This is רבי's view. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says: once he washed at the start of his service, he does not need to wash again, even for the next ten days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא with the same two תנאים arguing. This time the כהן never stopped working through the night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier ברייתא the כהן washed and then stopped serving before the next day came. Here he serves straight through, and רבי still says the coming of morning cancels his washing. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says the washing lasts as long as he keeps serving, even for ten days.

keyTerms.meaning: In the morning, when daylight comes
From the start of his service

phrases.english: It is taught in another ברייתא:

phrases.aramaic: הָיָה עוֹמֵד וּמַקְרִיב עַל גַּבֵּי מִזְבֵּחַ
phrases.english: If he was standing and offering on top of the altar
all night, then in the morning
he requires washing of hands and feet.
These are the words of רבי.
רבי אלעזר son of רבי שמעון says:
Once he washed his hands and feet
at the start of the service,
even from now for the next ten days
phrases.notes: He means: as long as he keeps serving without stopping.

phrases.english: he does not need to wash.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a second ברייתא with the same argument as steps 25-26, applied to a case where the כהן served without stopping.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי: morning cancels the washing even for a כהן who served all night without stopping. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון: one washing at the start covers continuous service, even for ten days.

steps.title: Why both ברייתות are needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that we need both ברייתות. From the first alone we might think רבי agrees when there was no break. From the second alone we might think רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון agrees when there was a break.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both are needed. If we only had the first ברייתא, we might say רבי ruled that way there because the כהן stopped between services. Here, where he did not stop, we might say רבי agrees with רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון. And if we only had this ברייתא, we might say רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון ruled that way here because there was no break. In the other case he might agree with רבי. So both are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers an unspoken question: why repeat the same argument twice? It shows that each case teaches something the other one could not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first case has a break in the service, and that is the strongest case for רבי. The all-night case has no break, and that is the strongest case for רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון. Having both cases shows that each תנא holds his view even in the case that is hardest for him.
steps.confusionAlert: The word בְּהָא ('in this case') points to different ברייתות in the two halves. In the first half it means the all-night ברייתא; at the end it means the first ברייתא.

phrases.english: And both are needed;
for if it had taught us only the first one,
phrases.notes: The first one is the ברייתא from step 25: he washed by day, and then the night passed.

phrases.english: in that case רבי says so,
because he stopped between one service and the next;
but in this case, where he did not stop,
I might say רבי agrees
with רבי אלעזר son of רבי שמעון.
And if it had taught us only this case,
phrases.notes: Here 'this case' means the all-night ברייתא.

phrases.aramaic: בְּהָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן;
phrases.english: in this case רבי אלעזר son of רבי שמעון says so;

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בְּהָא – אֵימָא מוֹדֵי לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי;
phrases.english: but in that case, I might say he agrees with רבי;
so both are needed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the ברייתא in step 27 is not just a repeat of steps 25-26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: each case teaches something the other does not
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Each תנא might agree with the other in the case that is weaker for his own view.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both תנאים keep their views in both cases, with or without a break.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי says morning always cancels the washing, even when the כהן served all night with no break. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says the night passing never cancels the washing, even when the כהן stopped between services.

steps.title: רבי's source: בגשתם
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for רבי's reason and answers that it comes from the word בגשתם, 'when they come near'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is רבי's reason? Because it is written: 'when they come near.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where רבי's view comes from and points to the word בגשתם in the פסוק about washing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק requires washing 'when they come near' to the מזבח. רבי reads this as every new day of coming near, so each morning needs a new washing.

keyTerms.meaning: When they come near (to the מזבח)

phrases.english: What is the reason of רבי?
Because it is written: 'when they come near.'
phrases.notes: שמות 30:20

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks for the פסוק behind רבי's view in the argument.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word בגשתם, read as each new day of coming near.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's source: בבואם
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's reason: the word בבואם, 'when they go in'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון? Because it is written: 'when they go in.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון uses a different word in the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'When they go in' to the אהל מועד suggests one washing for one entry. As long as the כהן keeps serving, it counts as the same entry, so he does not need to wash again.

keyTerms.meaning: When they go in (to the אהל מועד)

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן?
phrases.english: What is the reason of רבי אלעזר son of רבי שמעון?
Because it is written: 'when they go in.'
phrases.notes: The same פסוק, שמות 30:20.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the other תנא's source, which comes from the same פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word בבואם: one washing per entry, which lasts through continuous service.

steps.title: What does רבי do with בבואם?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי: the word בבואם is also in the פסוק, so how does he explain it?
steps.simpleTranslation: But for the other one too, it is written 'when they go in'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רבי deals with the word that רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון relies on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both words are in the same פסוק. If בבואם teaches that one washing lasts, רבי needs to explain what that word is there for in his view.

phrases.english: And the other one too,
phrases.notes: 'The other one' is רבי.

phrases.english: isn't it written 'when they go in'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי using the word from step 30.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי must explain the word בבואם, which seems to teach that one washing lasts.

steps.title: בבואם stops us from washing before every act
steps.stepSummary: Answer: without בבואם we would think a כהן must wash before every single act of service. בבואם teaches that one washing per day is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the תורה had written only 'when they come near' and not 'when they go in,' I would have said he must wash for each and every coming near. So the Merciful One wrote 'when they go in.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that רבי does use the word בבואם, but for a different lesson.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On its own, בגשתם could mean every act of service needs its own washing. בבואם limits that to one washing for the whole service. רבי still uses בגשתם to say the washing ends with the day, so each new day needs a new washing.

keyTerms.meaning: Each and every coming near (each act of service)

steps.whatToRemember: Both תנאים use both words. רבי says בבואם means not every act needs washing, but each day does. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says one washing lasts through continuous service.

phrases.english: If 'when they come near' had been written
and 'when they go in' had not been written,

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה אָמֵינָא: עַל כׇּל גִּישָׁה וְגִישָׁה;
phrases.english: I would have said: for each and every coming near;
so the Merciful One wrote: 'when they go in.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 31.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the word another job: it limits a reading that would be too strict
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every single act of service would need its own washing.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי, בבואם teaches one washing for the service, and בגשתם teaches that each new day needs a new washing.

steps.title: What does the other opinion do with בגשתם?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון: the פסוק also says בגשתם, so how does he use that word?
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one, too: isn't it written 'when they come near'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks the same kind of question on רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון that it just asked on רבי. He builds on בבואם, so what does he learn from בגשתם?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each opinion picked one word from the פסוק as its source. A word in the תורה is not extra, so each side must explain what the other word teaches. The challenge is now aimed at רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one (the other opinion)
When they come near (to the מזבח)

phrases.english: And the other one, too:
phrases.notes: "The other one" is רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, who learned his rule from בבואם.

phrases.english: isn't it written "when they come near"!
phrases.notes: שמות 30:20

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors step 31: that question was asked on רבי, and this one is asked on רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's reading of the פסוק
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If he learns his rule from בבואם, the word בגשתם still needs a purpose in his view.

steps.title: בגשתם rules out an empty entrance
steps.stepSummary: First answer: without בגשתם, we would think a כהן must wash even when he enters with no plan to do any service.
steps.simpleTranslation: If only 'when they go in' were written, and not 'when they come near', I would have said a כהן must wash even for an entrance with no purpose.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a first answer for רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון. בגשתם limits the washing to a כהן who is coming to do service.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בבואם alone sounds like any entering at all calls for washing. Adding בגשתם, coming near to serve, would narrow it to entering for a real purpose. That would give בגשתם a job in his view.

keyTerms.meaning: An empty entrance, going in without planning to do any service
I would have said (a mistaken first thought)

phrases.english: If "when they go in" had been written
and "when they come near" had not been written,
I would have said:
even for an empty entrance.
phrases.notes: He means the כהן would need to wash even if he just walks in without doing any service.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי כְּתִיב ״בְּבוֹאָם״ וְלָא כְּתִיב ״בְּגִשְׁתָּם״ – הֲוָה אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 33.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns a limiting job to the extra word
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any entrance, even one with no service, would require washing.
steps.terutzMaskana: בגשתם limits washing to a כהן who comes to serve.

steps.title: The פסוק already says לשרת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects that answer: the word לשרת, 'to serve', already shows that an empty entrance does not need washing.
steps.simpleTranslation: For an empty entrance?! But it is written 'to serve'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the answer it just gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same פסוק says לשרת, 'to serve'. That word already tells us the washing is for service. So nobody would think an empty entrance needs washing, and בגשתם is not needed for that. The גמרא still needs a different job for בגשתם.

keyTerms.meaning: To serve, to do the עבודה

phrases.english: For an empty entrance?!
But it is written "to serve"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 34.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole first answer for בגשתם
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The word לשרת already teaches that an empty entrance does not need washing, so בגשתם would be extra.

steps.title: בגשתם teaches רב אחא בר יעקב's rule
steps.stepSummary: New answer: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון needs בגשתם for a rule taught by רב אחא בר יעקב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he needs 'when they come near' for the teaching of רב אחא בר יעקב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer for what בגשתם teaches. It points to a rule of רב אחא בר יעקב, which it quotes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the 'empty entrance' answer failed, the גמרא finds a different use for the word. This line only names the source. The content comes right after.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (brings a new answer after the old one was rejected)

phrases.english: Rather, he needs "when they come near"
for the teaching of Rav Acha bar Yaakov.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer that was rejected in step 35.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the word a different purpose
steps.terutzMaskana: בגשתם is the source for רב אחא בר יעקב's rule.

steps.title: The second washing is done while dressed
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב: everyone agrees the second washing is done while wearing the בגדי כהונה, because בגשתם describes someone missing only the coming near.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב אחא בר יעקב said: Everyone agrees that for the second washing, he washes while dressed. The פסוק says 'or when they come near', which means someone who is missing only the coming near. That excludes someone who is still missing both dressing and coming near.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רב אחא בר יעקב's rule and shows how it comes from בגשתם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'When they come near' describes a כהן whose only remaining step is to approach the מזבח. Everything else, including getting dressed, must already be done. So a כהן who has not yet dressed is not ready to wash, and the second washing must happen while he is dressed.

keyTerms.meaning: The second washing of hands and feet

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, בגשתם teaches that the second washing is done after the כהן is dressed, because only coming near should be left.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how the order of steps in the עבודה can be learned from a single word in the פסוק.

phrases.english: As Rav Acha bar Yaakov said:
Everyone agrees about the second washing
phrases.notes: This is the כהן גדול on יום כיפור, who washes more than once as he changes clothes.

phrases.english: that he washes while he is dressed;
for the verse says: "or when they come near":

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְחוּסָּר אֶלָּא גִּישָׁה בִּלְבַד,
phrases.english: someone who is missing only the coming near,
this one is excluded:
the one who is missing both dressing and coming near.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב: הַכֹּל מוֹדִים בְּקִידּוּשׁ שֵׁנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the teaching that step 36 pointed to.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The second washing must be done while the כהן is dressed, because בגשתם describes someone missing only the coming near.

steps.title: Why does the פסוק say להקטיר אשה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the next words of the פסוק, להקטיר אשה, come to teach.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'To burn a fire-offering': why do I need it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next words in the same פסוק. This line sets up a new question, and the answer will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word of the פסוק has now been given a job, so להקטיר אשה seems extra. The גמרא asks what it adds to the washing rules.

keyTerms.meaning: To burn a fire-offering on the מזבח

phrases.english: "To burn a fire-offering":
why do I need it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining בבואם, בגשתם and לשרת, the גמרא moves to the next words of the פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the words להקטיר אשה add to the washing rules
